incidents.victim: Cyprus-based airline, telecom providers, critical-infrastructure organizations, and a government entity (expanding to Saudi Arabia healthcare organizations)
incidents.vector: Phishing using an AI-generated fake resume that links to a backdoor hosted on a public file-storage site, with command-and-control routed through a decentralized file-sharing network.
incidents.impact: An Iranian intelligence-linked group used the backdoor and a follow-on toolkit to gain footholds for reconnaissance at Cypriot government, airline, telecom and critical-infrastructure organizations, later expanding the same campaign to healthcare targets in Saudi Arabia.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a limited subset of FinCEN's internal systems; the FBI, CISA and third-party forensic examiners are investigating.
incidents.impact: FinCEN took some systems offline as a precaution and extended filing deadlines; the Bank Secrecy Act e-filing portal remains operational and there is no evidence yet of a breach of beneficial-ownership databases.

incidents.victim: Government, telecommunications and financial-sector organizations targeted using the ARTEX framework
incidents.vector: State-backed hacking groups have integrated an open-source agentic AI penetration-testing framework into their toolsets to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks and web-application exploitation.
incidents.impact: Microsoft reports Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored groups used the framework to search for exposed secrets, enable supply-chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems; the tool has also been tied to attacks on South Korean and Japanese financial institutions and a breach affecting U.S. intelligence agencies.

incidents.victim: At least 22 organizations in energy, transportation, financial services and government
incidents.vector: AI-enabled campaign targeting internet-facing security-management servers at a major firewall vendor.
incidents.impact: Compromised at least 22 organizations across the UK, US, France, Germany, Australia, China and India.

incidents.vector: AI-assisted cyberattacks against banking and payments infrastructure.
incidents.impact: India's CERT-In warned the attacks triggered unauthorized financial transactions at banks, fintechs and technology providers supporting government-linked payments and vendor payouts.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a shared third-party marketing vendor.
incidents.impact: Customer marketing data, including email addresses, was taken; both companies said the incidents were unrelated to separate technical outages reported the same week.

incidents.vector: 13 malicious NuGet packages disguised as UI controls were distributed through fake "take-home" recruitment coding assessments on GitHub, side-loading malware via a Windows system binary during normal builds.
incidents.impact: The campaign stole Chrome browser credentials and cookies and could deliver additional payloads, exposing source code, SSH keys and cloud tokens on compromised developer machines.

incidents.vector: Backdoors planted in telecom infrastructure run malicious signaling-protocol commands over SS7 and Diameter networks.
incidents.impact: Enables tracking of subscriber locations, collection of device data, and interception of calls and SMS traffic against selected targets; the group has been active since early 2025.

incidents.vector: Attacker used a forgotten cloud access key, originally issued to a third-party AI service provider, to enter the company's cloud environment, then deployed an AI-powered penetration-testing framework to escalate access.
incidents.impact: Attacker accessed Barracuda's internal network and other cloud environments for nearly two days before containment.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to FIFA's Microsoft cloud environment.
incidents.impact: A cybercriminal group claims to have stolen 12 GB of data including identity/immigration documents and financial and legal records; after a failed extortion attempt, the group published the stolen data.

incidents.vector: Hacker accessed internal company systems.
incidents.impact: Attacker obtained limited account metadata, including usernames, emails and account timestamps; 1Password says vault data and passwords were never accessed.

incidents.victim: 18 EU politicians, law-enforcement officials and journalists
incidents.vector: A pro-Kremlin hacktivist group published personal information gathered on high-profile targets.
incidents.impact: Victims include Italy's Foreign Minister, Eurojust's president, Europol's cybercrime chief, Germany's federal police president, and journalists who cover Russian hacking and influence operations.

incidents.victim: CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence
incidents.vector: Breach of an unclassified open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system shared by both agencies.
incidents.impact: Exposed unclassified data and could reveal what analysts were searching for and tracking; officials say classified networks and information were not involved.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; FBI Director Patel declined to detail the intrusion method, citing an active investigation.
incidents.impact: Breach of the national database used for warrants, fugitives, missing-persons cases and background checks; the second breach at the FBI in recent months following a September attack.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of a 9.3-severity vulnerability to breach a hosted N-able server.
incidents.impact: Caused a week of outages to Mail Assure and SpamExperts dashboards; CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and directed federal agencies to patch by Thanksgiving.

incidents.victim: Equinor, Skagerak Energi and other Norwegian energy providers
incidents.vector: A secret-leaking flaw in classic Azure API Management instances allowed theft of API credentials.
incidents.impact: Norway's National Security Authority confirmed stolen credentials were used to access Norwegian energy-sector systems; Microsoft has patched the issue, but not all instances have been updated.

incidents.victim: T-Mobile, Cisco, Fujitsu, CNEX, Quintel and other US technology companies
incidents.vector: Theft of trade secrets through NDA violations, a stolen robot component, copied router source code, and a recruited researcher who provided access to a partner company's proprietary hardware.
incidents.impact: A federal jury convicted Huawei and three subsidiaries of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank and wire fraud, sanctions violations tied to Iran, and money laundering; sentencing is scheduled for September 2027.

incidents.victim: About 80 US newspapers, including Boston Herald, Denver Post, Newsday and the New York Daily News
incidents.vector: A web skimmer was hidden inside a shared third-party subscription-payment widget used across all affected sites, exfiltrating entered card data in real time over a live-streaming-style connection before users even clicked submit.
incidents.impact: The script loaded roughly 15,000 times per day for over a week, stealing payment-card data entered directly into forms; users who paid via Apple Pay, Google Pay or PayPal were not affected.

incidents.vector: Attacker gained access to one of the platform's vault keys.
incidents.impact: $12 million in assets stolen and laundered through a cryptocurrency mixing service; Chainflip suspended deposits, withdrawals and swaps, and its token lost a third of its value.

incidents.vector: In the underlying 2023 breach, attackers impersonated employees to the IT help desk to obtain temporary passwords, bypassing multi-factor authentication.
incidents.impact: New York regulators fined Rocket Mortgage and Mr. Cooper a combined $6.75 million for MFA and risk-assessment failures and for repeatedly reporting incidents late; attackers had stolen large amounts of customer data in the original breach.

incidents.vector: Attackers stole a developer access key from old logs after breaching Iceland's largest web hosting provider.
incidents.impact: $13.5 million in tokens stolen from the Wagyu platform; the underlying hosting breach also knocked more than 20,000 unrelated websites offline.

incidents.victim: Organizations and developers using the Microsoft Agent Framework Python package
incidents.vector: Two unauthorized versions of the agent-framework Python meta-package were uploaded to PyPI containing credential-stealing code that runs whenever Python starts.
incidents.impact: Any machine, container or CI job that installed the malicious versions should be treated as compromised and have all accessible credentials rotated; Microsoft took the GitHub repository offline pending further review.

incidents.victim: 178 websites including BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom
incidents.vector: Exploited a vulnerability in a website A/B-testing platform to inject malicious JavaScript into customer sites, delivering card-skimming and cryptocurrency-swapping malware plus iOS exploit chains.
incidents.impact: Malware was served to visitors of 178 sites for roughly 16-24 hours before the vulnerability was patched; researchers estimate about $7,500 in stolen cryptocurrency plus an unknown number of stolen payment-card records.

incidents.victim: Santos Port Authority (Port of Santos, Brazil)
incidents.vector: Ransomware encrypted data at South America's largest port, likely via a malicious email or compromised website; coincided with a separate data-center power outage.
incidents.impact: Disrupted the port authority's ERP systems and customer-facing online services for over two weeks; data created after Oct. 31 could not be recovered from backups.
